correctness.rationale: The piecewise-C1 radial map has exterior derivative (I-u phi^T)/r. Its exact weighted infinity and one induced matrix norms are weighted row and column sums. Sharp Hölder equalities yield the two independent scalar maxima with exponents p and p′. Boundary limits and segment integration identify these derivative suprema with the global Lipschitz constants. Scalar first-order monotonicity ensures uniqueness; elementary sharp scalar bounds and positivity of weights prove dimension reversal and balancing. The included verification program reproduces 4371 deterministic assertion groups but is not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Rieffel 2005, Section 8 and Christianson et al. 2022 treat same-norm radial constants; Thele 1974 and Kapoor–Mathur 1983 as represented by inspected abstracts likewise treat same-norm geometry. The new complete sharp pair measures the \(\ell_p\)-ball radial map in distinct weighted coordinate metrics for every real \(p\), and includes explicit norm witnesses and dimension-dependent conjugate-order reversal. The previously recorded exact Euclidean \(p=2\) weighted result is a covered special case and not itself asserted original. No inspected source implies the broader all-\(p\) cross-norm claim; historical full-text access remains imperfect.
residual_risks: Thele 1974 and Kapoor–Mathur 1983 historical full papers were not accessible in full text. Their available formulations are native-norm; a hidden general equivalence cannot be excluded.
An earlier mixed-norm nonlinear radial-projection theorem under different language may exist despite the searches.
Semantic ranked search cannot prove uniqueness, and the source comparison cannot rule out unpublished work.

value.rationale: The dual weighted coordinate norms are natural error models for radial normalization into an ell_p ball; their exact optimal Lipschitz constants for all real p, dimensions and positive weights are not implied by same-norm radial theory or the p=2 subcase. The theorem supplies explicit extremizers, unique best balancing and a conjugate-exponent dimension-growth reversal between small and large dimension. This constitutes a motivated complete sharp-invariant computation with nontrivial geometric dependence, not an arbitrary finite slice.
